text: Shredder 是 DSH Web 客户端的会话管理插件，在原生已归档会话菜单中添加红色“彻底删除”操作。用户点击两次确认后，主机端停止会话工作、删除会话日志目录并清理归档记录；如果实例仍在忙碌，插件会延后完成收尾。适合需要从归档列表永久删除单个会话的用户。无需 API 密钥或外部服务。安装在支持 bundle 的 profile 中。

Shredder adds a delete action to archived session menus in DSH web. A second click confirms; the host endpoint stops session work, removes the session directory, and clears its archive record. Busy sessions may need deferred cleanup. No API key or external service is required.
想从已归档会话的菜单里彻底删除一个会话。
DSH 的归档会话怎么永久清掉？
I want a delete action for an archived DSH session.
Shredder 的功能「删除已归档会话」：在原生会话菜单中为归档会话显示红色删除项；点击一次进入确认，再点击发送删除请求。主机端停止会话工作、删除日志目录并清理归档记录。
Shredder 的功能「处理残留归档记录」：当会话日志已不存在但归档 ID 仍保留时，删除操作会清除该归档记录；需要等待驻留实例收尾时，插件会安排后台复查。

dsh-shredder README · dsh-shredder：One red **Shred session** row inside DeepSeek Harness's own session menu, for permanently deleting a session you have already archived.

`dsh-shredder` is a community plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/) (`dsh`). It is not an official DeepSeek AI product.

dsh-shredder README · What it does：- Adds one row to the **native** "…" menu of a session row, right below **Unarchive session**.
- The row only appears when that session **is archived** — an ordinary session never shows a delete option here.
- Two-step inline confirmation: the first click turns the row into **Confirm permanent delete**, the second one deletes. Closing the menu resets it.
- On success the session is gone from every surface: the workspace list, the ungrouped list and the archive set.
- If the log file is already gone but the id is still stuck in the archive set (a stale archive record), the same row just clears the record instead — and says so.

dsh-shredder README · What it deliberately does not do：- **No archive panel, no extra page, no sidebar entry.** Archived sessions are shown by dsh itself inside the workspace they belong to; the native **View options → hide / show / only archived** filter already lists them. This plugin adds the one action that dsh does not provide, in the place where the action belongs.
- **No bulk delete, no search, no preview, no restore-and-open.** If you want an archive *workspace*, see the alternatives below.
- **No trash can, no undo.** "Shred" here means the session directory is unlinked from the filesystem; it does not overwrite disk blocks. Recovering a shredded session needs a file-recovery tool at best.
section: What it deliberately does not do

dsh-shredder README · Requirements：- dsh **0.2.0-rc.2** verified. Older hosts are supported through a fallback path (they lack the public `unarchiveSession`), but only the current release is measured.
- A profile that loads bundles (the shipped `desktop` / `web` profiles).

dsh-shredder README · Install：```powershell
   & "<dsh install>\resources\runtime\pnpm\bin\pnpm.cjs" --dir "$HOME\.dsh\profiles\<profile>" add "file:C:/plugins/dsh-shredder"
   ```

On the desktop app the profile is `desktop`. `dsh --profile desktop --dump-config` is refused there (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`), so verify by restarting and opening a session menu.

dsh-shredder README · Updating after you edit the source：`file:` dependencies are installed as a **copy**, not a link. Deleting the installed copy and running `pnpm install` (even with `--force`) does **not** re-copy it — pnpm answers `Already up to date` and the plugin silently stops being mounted. Re-declare the dependency instead, and check bytes:
section: Updating after you edit the source

text:
dsh-shredder README · Updating after you edit the source：```powershell
Remove-Item "$HOME\.dsh\profiles\<profile>\node_modules\dsh-shredder" -Recurse -Force
& "<pnpm.cjs>" --dir "$HOME\.dsh\profiles\<profile>" add "file:C:/plugins/dsh-shredder"   # must print `Packages: +1`
```

Then compare `lib/*.js` between the two trees (sha256), and restart.
section: Updating after you edit the source

text: dsh-shredder README · Uninstall：Remove the `dependencies` entry and the `dsh.profile.bundles` entry, run install again, restart. To stop mounting it without uninstalling, remove only the `bundles` entry — the bundle layer then never composes. Do **not** add a user-level `- id: shredder / disabled: true` line for that: an id that is not in the tree only makes every start print `patch: entry "shredder" not found` to stderr.

dsh-shredder README · How it works：| Half | File | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host | `lib/index.js` | one loopback HTTP endpoint |
| Client | `lib/client.js` | the menu row, injected into `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` at `order: 450` |
| Mount | `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle-layer `insert` row (`id: shredder`) |

| Method | Path | Body | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/dsh-shredder/delete` | `{ sessionId }` | `{ ok, action: 'deleted' \| 'record-only', … }` |

Deletion order is part of correctness:

dsh-shredder README · How it works：1. Ask the owners to stop — the official `workspace/session-stop` seam (agent turn, jobs, subagents, schedule).
2. `flush` the live session so buffered events reach disk.
3. Evict the resident instance from the session store, so every tab drops its row and no late write can rebuild the directory.
4. `WorkspaceEntity.detachSession` — drop the workspace membership slot. Archiving keeps the slot on purpose (unarchive restores the position), so deleting the file first would make the session flash back into the workspace list.
5. Remove `<session root>/<project>/<id>/`.
6. Unarchive (official `workspaceRegistry.unarchiveSession`), which clears the archive record.
7. Background re-checks at +2s / +6s / +15s delete a directory that a late flush resurrected.

dsh-shredder README · Known boundaries：- **Irreversible.** Export anything you might want back before shredding.
- **Sometimes the row stays, and the archive flag is kept on purpose.** Clearing the archive record only makes sense once every browser tab has dropped the session row. That is guaranteed when the resident instance was evicted synchronously (`session/disposed` broadcast). It is *not* guaranteed when the instance was busy at that moment (the host defers the detach) or when the session is not resident in this process at all — in those two cases unarchiving would move a still-displayed row into the ordinary session list, and clicking it would read a deleted log ("session not found"). So the endpoint deletes the file and reports `recordHeld: true` instead. The browser half then re-pulls the official session list through the client `sessions` service (`refresh()` → `session.list`, whose merge keeps only ids the host still reports, so the vanished row drops out) and **only afterwards** re-issues the request to clear the record — no reload or restart needed. If that entry point is missing or the re-pull fails, the row simply stays archived; the background pass clears a deferred

dsh-shredder README · Alternatives, if you want more than one row：The plugin store has fuller archive managers — `@michengai/dsh-archive-manager` (a whole Settings page: title and content search, favorites, bulk restore, batch cleanup, log diagnosis), `dsh-better-archive` (settings section plus a right-sidebar archive tab, built on the host's own `Menu` / `RiskConfirmation`), and `dsh-archive-manager` (sidebar footer panel with agent teardown). They overlap with what this plugin does and go far beyond it. Pick this one only if what you wanted was "the delete option, in the menu, without another page".
section: Alternatives, if you want more than one row
